properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): an operations incident on an asset the design never modelled has one legal home, the Project, and only /jot's instruction names it. record_finding refuses an unmodelled subject and advises "use its constructor" (model the asset first, mid-incident), and a defect finding, once recorded, is read by no part of the loop: the reader dec:defects-are-temporal-facts called "the next increment" was never built
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28 (hxm_program hub, 2026-09-28, reflow2 0.73.0) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed. Issue F-30. Asset, host and device names are redacted because this export is public.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "Operations incidents have nowhere cheap to live in the design. The [motion-axis] incident had a precise asset ([a motion controller, one axis, an IOC on a host]), a timeline, three status decodes, five candidates and a resolution. Not one of those things exists as a node. search_design for a [beamline] motion component returned the zmq-proxy chain and HEX nodes. Recording it in the graph would have meant first designing the [beamline's] motion system (Components for controllers, axes and IOCs, then allocations) mid-incident, with the hutch waiting. So it went to a markdown file, which is correct for today and means the design cannot see the most operationally valuable record of the day." EXPECTED: an incident lands in the design in about the time it takes to say it, and the next incident on the same asset finds it. NOT AFFECTED: the root-cause skill itself ran on the incident and shaped it (the reporter: it "earns its place even when the graph holds nothing"). A finding about a node that IS modelled records in one call.

② PRECEDENT (search_design on the raw words, then on "operational know-how" and "incident ... asset stub"): no earlier record of an operations incident. Near records:
· dec:defects-are-temporal-facts (accepted) scopes a defect to one "found by USING a built capability", with subject_id "the node it indicts". Its own text: "Nothing in the LOOP reads these yet ... That reader is the next increment and it is a Rust change."
· dec:idea-a-one-word-capture-for-something-to-come-back-to (decided 2026-09-16; /jot tags shipped in #586, 2026-09-24, so they were served on 0.73.0). It was built from Anthony's own beamline instance and assumed "THE SUBJECT IS KNOWN AND NAMED ... a default subject of the Project is the fallback for the rare case, not the norm." In an operations hub the rare case is the norm.
· dec:idea-the-thing-you-need-to-point-at-is-usually-not-a-node-yet: five sightings, three of them from this hub (a file as a cause, a failure class, a repository).
· dec:idea-operational-know-how-is-a-design-rule-governing-the-environment-and-the-routing-table-should-say-so: this hub's F-05, 2026-08-26.

③ CANDIDATES, from the bones:
(A) INTENT. No requirement asks that an operations incident be capturable. The accepted defect mechanism assumes a modelled, built subject, so hardware the design never described is outside its intent by construction. The requirements that do feed reality back (req:a-person-feeds-results-back-by-upload-chat-or-folder and its siblings) are about test results landing "against what they test".
(B) CONTRACT. record_finding's subject must resolve, an unmodelled asset cannot be one, and the refusal points at modelling.
(C) ROUTING. A one-call path exists (the Project as subject, the asset named in the statement), but the instructions on the incident path never name it.
(D) SURFACING. Even once recorded, an open defect finding is read by nothing in the loop.
(E) OUTSIDE REFLOW2. The hub's own house rules (a troubleshooting archive with a fixed shape, a file-home ratchet) put incidents in files.
(F) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG. A cheap path existed and the session did not know it.

④ WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM: F predicts an instruction on the incident path (the root-cause skill, record_finding) that names a fallback subject, and a recorded incident appearing in loop_status. B predicts a refusal on an unmodelled subject. C predicts the fallback is named only at the /jot door. D predicts no loop line for an open defect finding. E cannot be separated from here, because the hub's files were not read.

⑤ RESULTS, from the 0.74.0 binary on a scratch store holding only a Project:
· record_finding on an unmodelled asset id was REFUSED: "no node with id ... exists under any type ... if you meant to CREATE this node, use its constructor." B HOLDS.
· The same finding with the Project as subject was accepted in one call. search_design on the asset's words returned it, and a second finding naming the same asset came back beside it, so accretion by text already works. F PARTLY HOLDS.
· The fallback is named in the jot skill ("None: the subject is the Project. Never ask for an id") and nowhere on the incident path. Root-cause step ⑧ says record_finding "hangs it off the node it is about", with no fallback, and its honest limits say it "can only offer candidates about what it MODELS". Jot frames itself as a note to come back to later, not as the record of an incident happening now. C HOLDS.
· loop_status after an open defect finding on the Project: no line; `next` carried only a gap line. The same sentence recorded as follow_up:issue was listed with settle_toward. On reflow2's own design, 349 of 364 defect findings carry no valid_to, and loop_status reads none of them. D HOLDS.
· No Requirement names an operations incident, a field fault or an asset not yet modelled. A HOLDS.
⇒ F is QUALIFIED, not refuted. The session could have recorded the incident in one call on the Project. Nothing on the path it was on said so, and the record would then have been visible only to a search.

⑥ CLASS: reflow2's recording paths are written DESIGN-FIRST. A record needs its subject to already exist as design content, and operations starts from the thing that broke, which usually does not exist yet. The instance here is an asset. The same class covers the file-as-cause (F-18), the failure class (O-10) and the repository (O-09) in dec:idea-the-thing-you-need-to-point-at-is-usually-not-a-node-yet, and the "subject is known" assumption /jot was built on. Test: would a fix at the class have stopped this hub's F-05 (2026-08-26, operational know-how went to a page) and F-18? Yes. Rewording root-cause step ⑧ alone would have stopped neither. A second, independent cause stacks on it: a defect finding is something the loop writes and nothing in the loop reads, the declared-and-read-by-nothing class this project names elsewhere.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE: no code changed. A test pinning the class would assert three things. First, every served instruction that tells an agent to record a finding names what to hang it on when the thing is not modelled. Second, a finding on an unmodelled subject is refused with a reply naming that fallback, not only "use its constructor". Third, an open defect finding appears in some loop read until a valid_to or an INVALIDATES edge closes it.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS. HELD: the incident's asset, timeline, candidates and resolution have no node; search finds nothing for an unmodelled asset; recording it with its structure means modelling the asset first. QUALIFIED: "nowhere cheap to live". A one-call record on the Project exists and search would have found it again. What is missing is an instruction on the incident path naming it, the incident's own shape (a timeline, and cause status apart from resolution), and any loop read that surfaces it. The idea is O-17, recorded separately.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED:
· whether the reporting session knew /jot existed;
· what the hub's own rules require of an incident record (its files were not read);
· whether a Project-level finding stays findable by search on a 500-node hub design (the ranking was measured on a two-finding scratch store);
· how many of reflow2's 349 defect findings without valid_to are in fact closed by INVALIDATES edges.
